value.body: A home care nurse looks after patients in their own homes: older people, bedridden patients, people recovering from surgery and those with long-term illness. Home healthcare companies, nursing agencies and hospital home-care units hire them, and some families hire nurses directly. A shift involves medicines, injections and dressings, monitoring vital signs, preventing bed sores and keeping the doctor and family informed.

items.label: Typical entry
items.note: Registration with the State Nursing Council is required

items.label: Shift pattern
items.value: Day, night or 24-hour live-in duties, depending on the patient

value.title: How you get in
value.body: After the diploma or degree and State Nursing Council registration, nurses apply to home healthcare companies or nursing agencies. Most employers prefer some hospital experience first, especially in ICU or post-operative care.

value.title: At a glance
items: Pay and terms depend on the agency and the patient's needs.
The work is often alone, without a ward team on hand.
Hospital experience makes it easier to move into hospital or overseas nursing later.
